title: Decide whether driving Tree and SectionedTree as navigation is supported
foundBy: session agent, while triaging five consumer reports for the repository owner
details:
Five of the records filed alongside this one come from driving Tree and SectionedTree as navigation sidebars rather than as file trees: the row alignment, the label overflow, the missing scroll into view, the forced per-section chrome, and the absent content-height mode.

The components are written for file trees. Nav sidebars want different defaults on nearly every axis, which is why each report arrives as a separate prop request.

The question is worth answering once, on the record, rather than per prop. If navigation is a supported use, the answer is probably a documented pattern or a variant that sets those defaults together, and the individual props follow from it. If it is not, the records should say so and the answer to a consumer is to compose primitives.

One of the reports raised this and nobody answered it. Filed so it is not re-litigated five times.

notes.text:
The repository owner adopted the stopping rule this branch had proposed and never had confirmed: fix the defects a consumer would hit, record everything else, and decide the rest at 0.3.0. This record is one of the six that wait, because each adds or changes a public prop, and `CONTRIBUTING.md` asks that the design be settled before the code is written.

They are one conversation rather than six, and this is the order they unlock in: CUI-014 first, because whether navigation is a supported use decides CUI-011; then CUI-012, because the `storageKey` convention decides CUI-010; then CUI-009 and CUI-011 together, which are both about sizing to content; and CUI-013 last, which stands alone. The Tooltip and MarkdownMinimap changes that already landed belong in the same conversation.

This is the first question of the six. Answering it either way stops the same request arriving once per prop.
